data.why: The app only reads committed data/processed/features.csv, data/raw/*.csv, models/*.joblib and reports/*.json; it never calls Earth Engine or Open-Meteo live and has no upload widgets, so nothing needs to be supplied.

goals: See which of the 36 field sites across Afghanistan, the Netherlands, and New Zealand are predicted to have vegetation stress in the latest 16-day period
Compare Random Forest vs. XGBoost predictions and their test accuracy/F1 metrics
Inspect a single location's NDVI history and stress-probability trend over time
Compare stress incidence, per-country model performance, and NDVI seasonality across the three countries
Check how much usable cloud-free satellite coverage each location actually has
Get a SHAP waterfall explanation of exactly how one specific prediction was calculated

review.summary: This tree describes the app accurately. The goal, phases and features match the README's purpose: forecast vegetation stress, judge model trust per model and per country, check satellite coverage, and explain single predictions. Most cited screens check out, but the GhazniCity SHAP evidence shows the wrong period, and the resulting 'inconsistency' note would file a false bug, so that and the static per-country table need correcting before filing.
